questions.q: Why does tempdb never get backed up, while master, msdb, and model do?
options: Tempdb is rebuilt from scratch every time the SQL Server service restarts, so it never holds anything that survives a restart
Tempdb backups are technically impossible in SQL Server
Only user databases like AdventureWorks ever need backups
Tempdb is the least important database, so it's simply skipped
questions.explain: Tempdb is scratch space rebuilt on every restart — there's nothing persistent in it to back up.

questions.q: What does the model system database do?
options: It stores SQL Server Agent job history
It holds all server-level login information
It's the template every new user database is created from
It's a reporting database used only by SSRS
questions.explain: Whatever settings (like collation or recovery model) are configured on model become the default for every database created afterward.

questions.q: A DBA wants to confirm last night's backup job actually succeeded. Which system database holds that history?
options: model
msdb
master
tempdb
questions.explain: msdb stores SQL Server Agent jobs, schedules, and backup/restore history.

questions.q: Which system database holds instance-level metadata like logins and linked servers, and where every other database's files live?
options: msdb
model
master
tempdb
questions.explain: master is the instance's own metadata store — the server won't even start without it.

questions.q: What is the central shift this course makes compared to T-SQL Development, per this lesson?
options: There is no shift — this course just repeats T-SQL Development
From T-SQL to Python exclusively
From SQL Server to a completely different database platform
From writing SQL to work with data, to using T-SQL to diagnose and fix problems with SQL Server itself
questions.explain: This course explicitly assumes the T-SQL language foundation and redirects it at server diagnostics instead of business data.
